articleHeadline: Multidrug-resistant and virulence traits in genetically distinct vesicular Leptospira inhabiting farmland and sewage in Southern India
articleSummary: Multidrug-resistant and virulence traits were identified in genetically distinct vesicular Leptospira inhabiting farmland soil, stagnant water, and sewage in Southern India. Five environmental isolates from Site 1 near farmland include L. levettii SA-E5, L. kmetyi SA-E7, Leptospira sp. SA-E8, and L. koniambonensis SA-E9 from soil/water, while Site 2 near a wildlife enclosure yielded two L. interrogans strains, SA-L3 and SA-L4, from sewage. Purity confirmed by filtration/subculturing; cells appeared as typical spirochetes with extracellular vesicles on microscopy. 16S rRNA sequencing placed SA-E5/SA-E7 with L. levettii MCA2-B-A1 and L. kmetyi Bejo-Iso9; SA-E8 near L. andrefontaineae; SA-E9 near L. koniambonensis TK1-4; SA-L3/SA-L4 near L. interrogans KeTo and RGA. BOX- and ERIC-PCR showed genomic distinctness. Genome sizes span 4–4.8 Mbp; GC 35.1–44.8%. OrthoANI/dDDH values indicate close relatedness to respective references (e.g., SA-E5 98.1%/83.2%), with most isolates environmental except the clinical-linked L. interrogans strains. Findings reveal environmental reservoirs of virulent, possibly drug-resistant Leptospira in Indian farmland.

articleHeadline: Health alert: VSD, TNMA clash over project on anthrax burial site
articleSummary: TNMA plans to develop part of the Veterinary Investigation Farm at Kwabedu, housing anthrax burial sites, despite objections and legal advice. The Veterinary Services Department (VSD) warns this could trigger a national epidemic through exposure of humans and animals to deadly pathogens. Dr. Simon Gbene, Regional Director for Western and Western North, says officials ignored scientific warnings and that relocation assurances from the Regional Minister have not produced action. The farm, established in 1978 with EU funding, serves Volta, Eastern, Central, Western and Western North regions and supports the Regional Veterinary Laboratory in Takoradi. The disputed land contains anthrax burial sites from May 2024; international protocols require such sites to remain undisturbed for up to 100 years due to soil-spore persistence. About 75% of emerging/re-emerging infectious diseases originate from animals. The Assembly has no legal title; the VSD has petitioned the Attorney-General for action. Excavation has not started; fence demolition raises security concerns. Interventions urged by Health, Local Government, EPA, security agencies, civil society, and media.

articleHeadline: Phase-specific climatic sensitivities of under-five malaria in Ghana using epidemic modelling, NB-GAMs and SHAP explainability
articleSummary: Malaria in under-five children in Tarkwa-Nsuaem Municipality, Ghana, exhibits phase-specific climate sensitivities across latent, accelerated, and delayed transmission phases from January 2013–December 2023 (132 months). The study estimates a cumulative incidence of 115,052 malaria cases (95% CI 107,390–125,844), with an inflection at ~75 months and a growth scale of 23.9 months. Severe malaria declines rapidly, with functional decline around month 44, while malaria-attributed deaths decline more slowly, near month 90. Incidence shows greatest climate sensitivity in the accelerated phase, with both temperature and rainfall linked to transmission; temperature associations remain significant even after excluding extreme rainfall months, whereas rainfall signals are more affected by extreme hydrological conditions. Mortality is temperature-sensitive primarily during the accelerated phase; rainfall effects are less consistent. SHAP analysis flags transmission phase, rainfall, and temperature as key predictors. Phase delineation and phase-specific NB-GAMs with explainability offer a framework for phase-targeted malaria surveillance and intervention planning.
